keyFindings.text: **"The Stop hook keeps nudging" overstates the code.** `takeNudge` reports only when the pending count exceeds the cursor, and lowers the cursor silently when a save consumed part of the queue; a session whose count stops rising is nudged once, not every turn. The recurring surface in real use is therefore the sweep's `pending` list printed at every save, not a repeating Stop message. The 002 description states the symptom as a repeating Stop nudge. keyFindings.text: **Answer-text matching is structurally impossible against any table the writer itself produces.** The decisions table has five columns and no answer column (`| ID | Decided | Why | Supersedes | Carried by |`), and `formatDecisionRow` emits exactly those five cells. So even for the writer's own record the only text that can ever be matched is the appendix's. A nine-column hand-written table (answer present) is the only table where answer matching is even conceivable, and no code parses one. keyFindings.text: **Appendix parsing accepts one style only.** `FIELD_LABEL_RE` anchors `Question:`/`Options:`/`Answer:` at column 0 with no leading marker, so a bolded or indented label parses to nothing, and `readUnkeyedExchangeIds` skips any item with an empty question or answer. A hand-written appendix that uses `**Answer:**` is invisible to the matching path that was built for hand-written appendices. The text comparison itself normalizes case and internal whitespace only — no punctuation, markdown or fuzzy handling. keyFindings.text: **Capture is silent by design, including when it drops a decision.** `normalizeAskUserQuestion` returns `[]` for any shape it does not recognize and drops process questions with no log line. Two consequences worth naming: a newer tool payload that keys `answers` by index rather than by exact question text yields zero records and no signal; and a product question whose header merely matches `worktree`/`branch`/`spec folder` is discarded as process bookkeeping. Multi-select answers are joined with `", "`, which is indistinguishable from a single option that contains a comma. keyFindings.text: **Four gaps 002 does not close, each with a cheap addition.** (a) The mapping lives in gitignored state, so it is per-machine — the plan names the cost but plans no mitigation; a committed, packet-local key→Q-id map would survive a re-clone. (b) Nothing invokes the matcher: the documented save path still runs the sweep only, so the same drift can reappear on the next captured answer unless `save.md`/`save-workflow.md` and the nudge text name the matcher. (c) Refusals must be counted and surfaced — the plan's own measurements show rows differing by shortened options and `/ `-joined line breaks, so "pending = 0" is the wrong handoff criterion; "pending = reported refusals" is honest. (d) Findings 7, 8, 13 and 14 (record/log divergence, orphan session queues, row/appendix divergence, no release path) are untouched by 002 and are not obviously owned by any other child. keyFindings.text: **`checkpoints.tsv` is not a runner artifact, so 006's headline gate has no producer.** 065's per-runtime evidence is `result.json`, `actions.jsonl`, `raw-pane.log`, `setup.log`, both repository snapshots, `matrix.md`, and per turn `screen.txt`, `question-N.txt` and `check.txt`. There is no `checkpoints.tsv` and no per-stage row anywhere. Yet 006's T007 verifies "`wc -l < checkpoints.tsv` prints 13", AC-005 requires 13 rows each with a verdict and an evidence path, and the plan's evidence store lists the file as if the run yields it. 006 must own the derivation (merge `result.json` + `actions.jsonl` + `check.txt` per turn into rows) and say so; the plan instead says the runner "runs the checkpoint and saves the pane". The *runner* that executes it is `002-conversation-runner`. 006's T001 is blocked on the whole packet: "Wait for the shared conversation runner and its scenario format". Only the *run* tasks need 002; the scenario authoring task (T004) needs only 001, because the validator is what checks the file. The decision-capture state directory 006 most needs to protect is gitignored, so 006's check is blind to exactly the writes it exists to catch, while the runner would have caught them. 006 should cite the runner's snapshots as its evidence path instead of re-running a weaker command. **Hard conflict: 006's stage S12 cannot live in the same scenario file or the same run as S0 to S11.** S12 needs a *second* on-disk project (`$K`) with `SYSTEM_DECISION_CAPTURE_DISABLED=1`. The format gives one top-level `env` per script, the runner takes one `--scenario` and one `--scratch` per invocation, and a second fenced `json conversation` block is rejected as `CONVERSATION_SCRIPT_INVALID`. So either S12 becomes a second scenario file plus a second runner invocation, or 065 must accept per-runtime/per-turn `env` or a `reset` action. As written, 006's REQ-001 and AC-001 ("13 stage rows S0 to S12" in one file) and AC-005 (13-row `checkpoints.tsv` from one run) are unsatisfiable. [SOURCE: specs/sk-doc/authoring-modes-and-playbooks/004-conversation-playbook-scenarios/001-scenario-contract/spec.md:147] [SOURCE: specs/sk-doc/authoring-modes-and-playbooks/004-conversation-playbook-scenarios/002-conversation-runner/plan.md:78] [SOURCE: specs/system-speckit/043-decision-capture/006-live-conversation-test/plan.md:84] [SOURCE: specs/system-speckit/043-decision-capture/006-live-conversation-test/acceptance-criteria.md:56] **Confirmed** on all three constraints; the "S12 must therefore split" conclusion is **inferred** and is the direct consequence of them.

**S0 is structurally outside the runner: there is no turn, and therefore no `check`, before the project exists.** The runner's guard *requires* an already-prepared scratch project, and its `setup` commands run inside that prepared project while `check` runs only after a settled turn. 006's S0 is "build the scratch project, record baselines" with its own checkpoint. So S0 is 006's own pre-runner step (its T003), and its row in `checkpoints.tsv` can never come from the run. Consequence: the "13 rows from 13 stages" shape mixes one hand-produced row with twelve runner-produced turns. **The dependency is not circular, and 006 is not on 065's critical path — which is worth saying because 006's readiness gate reads as if it were.** 065's handoff criteria is its own MTP-007 scenario passing on Claude Code, and it names 043/006 as "the first consumer", not as its proof. So 065 can close without 006, and 006 waits. The cost is format risk, not deadlock: 065 designs the closed key set with no second consumer testing it, and the S12 conflict (finding 6) is the concrete shape that risk took. **The runner executes a turn's `check` with `bash -c` inside the project, with `CONVERSATION_REPO_ROOT`, `CONVERSATION_RUN_DIR` and `CONVERSATION_TURN_DIR` set, and stops that runtime's run at the first failed turn.** That is the only automated assertion surface 006 gets. Its S6 checkpoint ("4 rows, 4 items, 4 lines and 4 keys, no decided text equals its answer, process count 0, level line unchanged, queue still 3") is expressible as one `bash -c`, but the failure granularity is per turn, not per observable. [SOURCE: specs/sk-doc/authoring-modes-and-playbooks/004-conversation-playbook-scenarios/002-conversation-runner/spec.md:171] [SOURCE: specs/system-speckit/043-decision-capture/006-live-conversation-test/plan.md:78] **Confirmed.**

**The runner's turn schema is the operative constraint on 006's stage table.** A turn is `id`, `send` **or** `action` (`restart`/`compact`), `delay_ms`, `timeout_ms`, `questions[]` and a mandatory `check`; a turn without `check` is invalid. `questions[]` entries carry `match` (a regex), `answer` (`select`/`other`/`reply`) and `optional`. So 006's five observables for S2 ("1 line, 1 key, `Amber`, 1 nudge line, nudge file 1") must be collapsed into one shell command's exit status, and its five human actions must map onto `send`/`action`.
